ui_bugs.issue: Stale closure: shadow WS onmessage captures `channel` (state) at the time the WS was created. After the user switches channels, the closure still compares incoming msg.channel to the OLD channel, so unread/mentions counters do NOT increment for the previously-active channel. Repro: alice on #general, then alice clicks #help, then bob sends '@TEST_alice yo' to #general → no chat-unread-general badge appears even though the mention was in fact received and is rendered as chat-line-mentioned when alice returns to #general. First-hop cross-channel works because the closure value still matches.

rca of the issue: ChatTab in /app/frontend/src/pages/CommunityPage.jsx defines `onWsMessage = (ch, e) => { ... if (ch !== channel) { setUnread(...) } ... }` as an inline function and binds it ONCE per shadow socket via `ws.onmessage = (e) => onWsMessage(c, e)` inside the [buyerJwt, makerJwt, adminJwt] effect. The handler closes over the FIRST `channel` value (initial='general'). When the user later changes channel state, the WS handler is not re-bound, so the `ch !== channel` comparison uses the stale 'general'. Result: the first cross-channel hit (channel still matches) works, but any later cross-channel-to-the-original-channel never bumps unread/mentions. Fix: introduce `const activeChannelRef = useRef(channel)` updated inside a useEffect on [channel], then test `ch !== activeChannelRef.current` inside onWsMessage. Alternatively, list `channel` in the deps array and tear-down/rebuild sockets — but a ref is cheaper.
